note: For each domain: the eight steps of the workflow and the performing and ownership conditions for the eight judgment axes. Items, the results report and experience input all read this one file. `verify_targets` and `artifacts` are what the results report's action steps draw on, so they must be concrete here to avoid vague wording

domains.name: Policy and Program Planning

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A higher plan, an election pledge or the requirements of a public call arrive as a task

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: The higher plan, available budget and staff quota, deadline, precedents of similar programs

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: What not to do this time, what to do first, and the target range

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Turning goals into indicators, comparing options, dividing resources, making a schedule

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Spreadsheet tools, presentation tools, meeting notes, performance indicator definition tables

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: A full program plan, a performance indicator table, reasons for priorities, a schedule

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: The higher plan, past spending results, similar programs, achievement rate after the end

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If a goal is not achieved, separate whether the goal was too high or resources were not enough

verify_targets: Actual achievement rate after the end

J1.l2: Wrote down the targets and scope to cover this time in the given task
J1.l3: The scope I defined became the business scope as is

J2.l2: Turned goals into performance indicators measured with numbers
J2.l3: The indicators I set were used as evaluation criteria

J3.l2: Chose one of several options and allocated budget and staff
J3.l3: Budget or staff moved according to the allocation I decided

J4.l2: Chose and used a planning framework or an estimation method
J4.l3: The framework I chose was also used in the next planning

J5.l2: Kept a program plan or plan proposal as a document
J5.l3: Another person read the plan I left and carried it out

J6.l2: Compared two options with the same criteria
J6.l3: Changed the plan based on the comparison results

J7.l2: Narrowed the reason for a missed goal down to the goal or the resources
J7.l3: Confirmed that the same gap became smaller in the next plan

J8.l2: Presented the plan proposal in a meeting, explained it, and received agreement
J8.l3: My plan led to budget allocation or staff placement

org_outcomes.OC1: Plans with standards that apply in the same way across the country
org_outcomes.OC2: Plans with changes that residents feel right away
org_outcomes.OC3: Program plans linked to management evaluation indicators
org_outcomes.OC4: A project proposal and an execution plan
org_outcomes.OC5: Plans with review criteria and handling procedures
org_outcomes.OC6: Plans that reach the target groups with few resources
org_outcomes.OC7: Work plans that fit the scope of work set by the client

domains.name: Interpreting Laws and Regulations

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A case or inquiry where judgments differ arrives

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Acts, enforcement decrees and enforcement rules, guidelines, official interpretations, similar cases

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: The provisions that apply and do not apply, and the range of exceptions

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Comparing provisions, comparing cases, checking higher laws, writing the basis of interpretation

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Law search tools, court rulings and official interpretation materials, provision comparison tables, document editing tools

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: A review opinion, a provision comparison table, a record of the basis of interpretation, a reply to an inquiry

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Higher laws, past official interpretations, decisions in similar cases, results of appeals or lawsuits

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If an interpretation is reversed, narrow down which provision was read wrongly

tools: Court rulings and official interpretation materials
artifacts: Record of the basis of interpretation

J1.l2: Narrowed down and wrote the issues actually disputed in an inquiry
J1.l3: The issues I narrowed down became the review scope as they were

J2.l2: Broke down the requirements of a provision into items that can be checked
J2.l3: The requirement items I wrote were used as review criteria

J3.l2: Divided and decided the provisions that apply and the provisions that do not
J3.l3: A decision or reply was issued as I divided it

J4.l2: Chose and used a method or tool to find and compare provisions
J4.l3: The search order I set was also used in other reviews

J5.l2: Kept a review opinion or a provision comparison table
J5.l3: Another person used the review opinion I left as a basis

J6.l2: Checked my interpretation against higher laws or past official interpretations
J6.l3: Have changed a first interpretation after checking

J7.l2: Narrowed the reason an interpretation was reversed down to the provision level
J7.l3: Changed guidelines or forms so that the same misunderstanding would not happen

J8.l2: Explained review results and had them reflected in a decision or guidelines
J8.l3: My review was issued as the institution's official reply

org_outcomes.OC1: Official interpretations that apply in the same way across the country
org_outcomes.OC2: Interpretations that go out to residents directly as decisions
org_outcomes.OC3: Internal guidelines that are the basis of program spending
org_outcomes.OC4: Reviews that are the basis of proposals to improve systems
org_outcomes.OC5: Decision grounds that must hold up against appeals
org_outcomes.OC6: Program criteria that decide who meets the requirements
org_outcomes.OC7: Contract interpretations that prevent disputes about the scope of work

domains.name: Budget Planning and Spending

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: Budget guidelines and the requests of each department arrive together

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Past spending results, the total limit, mandatory spending, requested amounts for each program and their basis

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: Which programs to cut and by how much, and which programs to keep

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Estimating needs, checking unit prices, dividing allocations, setting a spending schedule

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Spreadsheet tools, a budget planning system, unit price tables, spending record lookup

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: A full budget plan, the calculation basis for each program, a spending plan, change records

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Past spending results, unit price standards, the total limit, spending rate after the end

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If spending is left over or short, separate whether the estimate was wrong or the schedule was delayed

artifacts: Calculation basis for each program amount
Remaining budget and reasons for carrying over

J1.l2: Wrote down the groups of programs to cover in this budget planning
J1.l3: The groups I divided became the budget planning units as they were

J2.l2: Broke down the words of a request into unit prices and quantities
J2.l3: The calculation basis I wrote was used as review material

J3.l2: Divided myself the amount for each program and kept the reasons
J3.l3: The amounts I divided were planned as they were

J4.l2: Chose and used a method to estimate needs or unit price standards
J4.l3: The estimation method I chose was also used in the next budget planning

J5.l2: Kept a budget plan or calculation basis as a document
J5.l3: Another person took the calculation basis I left and used it

J6.l2: Checked planned amounts against past spending results
J6.l3: Changed the allocation based on the check

J7.l2: Narrowed the reason for unspent or excess money down to the estimate or the schedule
J7.l3: Confirmed that the same gap became smaller in the next budget planning

J8.l2: Explained a budget plan at a review and received agreement
J8.l3: My calculation basis was reflected in the final budget

org_outcomes.OC1: Budget planning linked to the national fiscal management plan
org_outcomes.OC2: Budget planning that goes directly to programs residents feel
org_outcomes.OC3: Budgets tied to program goals and management evaluation
org_outcomes.OC4: Research funds spent and settled by project
org_outcomes.OC5: Budget planning for the costs of review and supervision
org_outcomes.OC6: Program costs that mix subsidies and donations

J1.l2: Wrote down separately the work to move this time and the work not to move
J1.l3: The scope I defined became the introduction scope as is

J2.l2: Turned what the person in charge said into a list of tasks for the system
J2.l3: The list I wrote became the requirements document

J3.l2: Separated myself the range to disclose from the range to hide
J3.l3: Disclosure decisions were issued as I divided them

J4.l2: Chose and used a method to draw workflows or write requirements
J4.l3: The form I set was also used in other programs

J5.l2: Kept a workflow diagram and a requirements document
J5.l3: The development or outsourcing side took the document I left and used it

J6.l2: Checked processing time or number of cases before and after introduction
J6.l3: Changed the requirements or the workflow based on the check

J7.l2: Narrowed the reason it is not used down to the requirements or the workflow
J7.l3: Fixed the requirements and confirmed that use increased

J8.l2: Explained the requirements and had them agreed as the scope of introduction
J8.l3: The disclosure range I set became the institution's standard

review_note: In public administration majors, roles that apply rules, roles that divide resources and roles that deal with people sit in one file. What keeps them apart is `required_axes`: policy, human resources, procurement and digital administration depend on interpreting requirements; civil complaints and disasters depend on failure and correction; laws, budgets, performance, data and accounting depend on comparison and verification. So even if six axes are confirmed, the evidence does not hold when a required axis of that domain is empty
